newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian yr/yr inflation falls to 2.1 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian yr/yr inflation falls to 2.1 pct in July.

text.p: Ivory Coast's year-on-year inflation rate fell to 2.1 percent in July, according to provisional figures from the national statistics institute. The rate in June was 2.3 percent.
The figures showed a 0.8 percent fall in prices on June, mainly due to a fall in the cost of food and cars.
The mean consumer price index (base year November 1992 to October 1993), was 148.76 in July. The figure in June was 149.9.
The year-on-year inflation rate in July 1995 was 11 percent.

The latest figures translate into an increase of 3.7 percent in prices in the first seven months of 1996. The rate for 1995 was 7.7 percent, slightly higher than the government's target of five percent. That compared to 32 percent in 1994.
An Economic and Financial Report, prepared to accompany the 1996 budget which was passed on March 8, said that the inflation target for 1996 was 4.9 percent.
Ivory Coast is one a group of French-speaking countries in Africa which devalued their common CFA franc currency by 50 percent in January 1994.
